title: Add a new disk and grow an LVM volume
tasks: extend a logical volume with a new disk

NEW_DISK.means: the new, empty disk, e.g. sdb

LV.means: the logical volume to grow, e.g. ubuntu-lv

SIZE.means: how much to add, e.g. 20G (at most the VFree shown by vgs)

MOUNT.means: where the volume is mounted, e.g. /var

steps.say: Find the new disk: TYPE disk, no partitions under it, no mount point.
Note the logical volume to grow.
Make the new disk an LVM physical volume. This overwrites anything on it.
steps.rollback: Undo while the disk is not yet in a volume group:

steps.say: Add the disk to the volume group. VFree in vgs grows.
steps.rollback: Undo while no volume uses the new space:

steps.say: Grow the volume and its filesystem in one step (-r).
steps.rollback: No simple undo: ext4 can only be shrunk unmounted, XFS never. Grow in small steps.

steps.say: The filesystem shows the new size.

pitfalls: Check the disk name twice: pvcreate on the wrong disk destroys its data.
